content: Industry analyses project that the utilization of high-strength steel will grow significantly, increasing from 13.05 million tons in 2026 to 17.76 million tons by 2031 [25] . Within this category, High-Strength Low-Alloy (HSLA) steels and Advanced High-Strength Steels (AHSS) are emerging as the materials of choice for premium wear parts . These advanced grades offer superior yield strengths and exceptional resistance to abrasive wear, which are critical durability metrics that differentiate top-tier brands from standard suppliers . To effectively compete, Alpha Industries SA must recognize that the differentiation of wear parts is increasingly reliant on metallurgical innovation rather than mere dimensional compatibility. The projected growth in HSLA and AHSS materials indicates that future market dominance will belong to brands that can successfully integrate these high-strength, durable, and environmentally conscious steel grades into their product lines. These material advancements are largely driven by concurrent progress in mining technology, equipment automation, electrification, and the integration of data analytics within the broader mining sector [34] [35] . While these technological trends highlight the increasing complexity and technical demands of wear parts globally, they also set the stage for understanding the evolving supply chain dynamics and competitive intelligence requirements for firms operating within South Africa's mining ecosystem. An analysis of the local versus imported mining wear parts ratio in South Africa from 2020 to 2023 illustrates a distinct and measurable shift in supply chain reliance. During this period, local production exhibited a consistent upward trajectory. In 2020, locally produced mining wear parts accounted for 40.0 percent of the total market share. This domestic output steadily increased over the subsequent years, culminating in a maximum value of 48.0 percent by 2023. Conversely, the reliance on imported components demonstrated a corresponding and proportional decline. In 2020, imported wear parts dominated the South African market at 60.0 percent, but this reliance decreased to a minimum of 52.0 percent by the end of 2023. Ultimately, the dynamics between local and imported mining wear parts in South Africa are shaped by a complex interplay of global technological advancements, historical supply chain realignments, and emerging collaborative business strategies.
